meta.scope: South Korea Batch 3 — Social structure depth (super-aged society, long-term care, gender, poverty/inequality) plus monetary/financial aggregates from BOK and supporting education/household indicators. Continues under locked definition.
meta.strategy_note: Addresses Korea’s extreme demographic transition (super-aged, ultra-low fertility already in Batch 2), care system, gender structure, inequality, and core monetary statistics. Parallel to the social and monetary clusters developed for Japan.

candidates.title: Super-aged society indicators and elderly population statistics
candidates.publisher: Statistics Korea (KOSTAT) / Ministry of Data and Statistics
candidates.description: Official statistics tracking the share of population aged 65+ (surpassed 20 % in 2025, formally entering super-aged status), old-age dependency ratios, and related demographic structure indicators. Derived from census, resident registration and population projections.
candidates.notes: Documents Korea’s rapid transition to a super-aged society. Complements the Vital Statistics and Population Projections nodes from Batch 2 and provides the high-level framing for long-term care, pension and labour-supply analysis.

candidates.title: Long-Term Care Insurance (노인장기요양보험) statistics and system performance
candidates.publisher: National Health Insurance Service / Ministry of Health and Welfare
candidates.description: Statistics on Korea’s Long-Term Care Insurance system (introduced 2008): number of certified beneficiaries, benefit expenditure, service types (home-based vs institutional), workforce, and trends in utilisation. Expenditure has risen sharply with population ageing.
candidates.notes: Korea’s social-insurance response to rapid ageing, parallel to Japan’s Long-Term Care Insurance node. Benefit costs have roughly doubled in recent years; data on certification, ‘old-old’ care patterns and preferred living arrangements are heavily cited in ageing-society policy.

candidates.title: Gender equality / women’s economic activity statistics and related white papers
candidates.publisher: Ministry of Gender Equality and Family / Statistics Korea / Ministry of Employment and Labor
candidates.description: Official statistics and periodic reports on gender gaps in employment, wages, unpaid care work, decision-making, and the National Gender Equality Index. Includes the White Paper on Women’s Economic Activity and related gender statistics.
candidates.notes: Captures the persistent gender structure of Korean society (employment gap, care burden, decision-making representation). Continuously referenced in labour, family and social-policy analysis. Parallel to Japan’s Gender Equality White Paper cluster.

candidates.title: Relative poverty rate and income inequality statistics (Gini, etc.)
candidates.publisher: Statistics Korea / Korea Institute for Health and Social Affairs (KIHASA) / related agencies
candidates.description: Official and research-based series on relative poverty (share of population below 50 % of median disposable income), Gini coefficients, and related distributional indicators, often with breakdowns by age (notably high elderly poverty) and household type.
candidates.notes: Korea’s relative poverty rate has hovered around 15 % in recent years, with elderly poverty markedly higher. These series are essential for social-cohesion and fiscal-sustainability analysis and complement the Household Income and Expenditure Survey from Batch 1.

candidates.title: Monetary and Liquidity Aggregates (M1, M2, Lf, L)
candidates.description: Monthly statistics on narrow money (M1), broad money (M2), liquidity of financial institutions (Lf) and overall liquidity (L). Core monetary indicators used for policy analysis and financial-stability assessment.
candidates.notes: Primary monetary statistics from the central bank. Continuously watched alongside policy rates and credit indicators. Parallel to Japan’s Monetary Base and related BOJ monetary series.

candidates.title: Flow of Funds Accounts / Financial Accounts
candidates.description: Quarterly and annual flow-of-funds / financial accounts showing the financial assets and liabilities of institutional sectors and the inter-sectoral financial flows.
candidates.notes: Complements the national accounts and Financial Statement Analysis with a full sectoral balance-sheet picture. Useful for analysing household debt, corporate leverage and the financial position of large business groups.

candidates.title: Education statistics (schools, enrolment, advancement) — Korean Educational Development Institute / KOSTAT / Ministry of Education
candidates.publisher: Korean Educational Development Institute (KEDI) / Statistics Korea / Ministry of Education
candidates.description: Annual and periodic statistics on schools, students, teachers, advancement rates, private tutoring (hagwon) participation and educational attainment. Reflects Korea’s high educational intensity and human-capital focus.
candidates.notes: Korea’s education system and private-supplement intensity are distinctive features of its social structure. These series link demographic change (shrinking school-age cohorts) to human-capital and labour-market outcomes.

candidates.title: Survey of Household Finances and Living Conditions (가계금융복지조사)
candidates.description: Annual survey measuring household assets, liabilities, income, expenditure and welfare indicators. Key source for wealth distribution, household debt and living-conditions analysis.
candidates.notes: Complements the Household Income and Expenditure Survey with balance-sheet (assets/liabilities) detail. Important for understanding household financial vulnerability and the interaction of housing wealth, debt and ageing.

candidates.title: Elderly / older-worker employment statistics
candidates.publisher: Statistics Korea (KOSTAT) / Ministry of Employment and Labor
candidates.description: Statistics on employment rates, desired retirement age and working conditions of persons aged 55–79 (and related older-age groups). Documents the high and rising labour-force participation of older Koreans.
candidates.notes: Distinctive feature of Korea’s ageing society: many older persons continue working well past traditional retirement ages, often from financial necessity. Links labour-force, pension and long-term-care analysis.

candidates.title: National Pension Service statistics / National Pension coverage and finances
candidates.description: Statistics on National Pension coverage, contributors, beneficiaries, benefit levels and fund finances. Central pillar of Korea’s public pension system under demographic pressure.
candidates.notes: Key social-security node under rapid ageing and low fertility. Continuously cited in fiscal-sustainability and intergenerational-equity discussions. Complements long-term care and elderly-employment series.
